 By Daniel Hood CloseText About Daniel 
 twitter accountingedit 
 mailto daniel.hood@arizent.com 
 linkedin daniel-hood-3494ab49 
 Published October 30, 2026, 5:31 p.m. EDT | Updated November 02, 2026, 11:27 a.m. EST 6 Min Read Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 What's at Stake: Whether average members can adapt aggregate industry roadmaps to their specific practices.
 Supporting Data: Approximately 7,500 accountants who provided input for the visioning project.
 Artificial intelligence looks set to cause enormous disruptions in the accounting profession — but now, thanks to the AICPA and CIMA, it's also set to help guide accountants through that disrupted future, with their Rise Navigator tool.
 Processing Content The AICPA's Rise Navigator offers a kind of GPS for accountants as they travel into the future.
 Artificial intelligence looks set to cause enormous disruptions in the accounting profession — but now, thanks to the AICPA and CIMA, it's also set to help guide accountants through that disrupted future, with their Rise Navigator tool.
 Rise Navigator is a Claude chatbot based on a vast trove of data specific to accounting that accountants can access for free online to ask for help with — well, anything.
 Tom Hood Tom Hood, executive vice president of business engagement & growth at the AICPA and CIMA, recalled demonstrating the tool to a sole practitioner at the Engage conference at the beginning of the summer: "He says, 'Well, what's it going to do for me?' I said, 'Why don't you ask it something?' So he says, 'OK, I'm a sole tax practitioner. This is what I'm doing. What advice would you give me in the next five years?' and it starts spitting out all this stuff and he's grabs his camera and he's trying to take pictures of it all. … He was blown away by it. And I thought, 'Wow, if it can help a sole practitioner, that's huge.'
 ( Listen: Tom Hood dives deeper into the uses of Rise Navigator on our podcast. )
 At another event in Europe, he recalled the CFO of a Swedish defense contractor asking the Navigator about the Swedish defense industry and how she should be thinking about her finance team, and the tool came back with advice about the capabilities she should be building in her team and the areas she should be focusing on — all in Swedish.
 "We're starting to see people loading in their strategic plans and asking it to evaluate their plan, and it does a killer job at that," Hood explained. "It says 'Here's what you should be doing more of. Here's what you should do less of. These are things you need to be thinking about. Here's how you position it.'"
 A new way to vision
 Rise Navigator is able to answer questions and provide advice on everything under the accounting sun — from broad strategic issues to narrow tactical ones — because of the robust foundation of data and insight it rests on.
 The tool is an offshoot of the Rise 2040 visioning project that the AICPA completed this year. The institute conducts these projects every 14 years or so, convening groups of accountants over several months to identify future trends and the ways the profession is going to have to change.
 The difference in Rise 2040 was that the organizers fed the input from approximately 6,000 accountants into AI, had it analyze them, and then shared that analysis with the groups for their reaction, creating a sort of feedback loop that refined the insights and projections the groups were coming up with — and almost inadvertently training the AICPA's LLM to become a valuable advisors to individual accountants.
 "We didn't really fully understand that that would be the potential of it," Hood said, "but because of the richness of the data set from all those members from all those sessions, and then it obviously goes outside a little bit to get things it can't find in our data, but it really can be a robust custom way of applying all that Rise research in real time to whatever situation you are in across the whole global profession."
 The Rise 2040 report came out this spring, and like its predecessors, it offered a roadmap for accountants for the next decade-and-a-half — but unlike them, it can be paired with the Rise Navigator to help individual practitioners and firm leaders and finance executives to customize it to their specific circumstances.
 "What we struggled with with Horizons and the Vision Project [the two previous visioning exercises] was making it applicable to the average member, and that's where the cultural inertia comes from, because you can publish this report that's in aggregate about what everyone thinks about the future, but then you go to that small practice in Illinois and they're saying, 'Well, wait a minute, this is what I do — I don't do the same as everybody else; how do I convert all this to me?'" Hood said.
 "Having a way of using the roadmap, the GPS to create your own roadmap that says, 'Here's a step-by-step cookbook for your practice, or your CFO office' — you've got something they can actually take back and do, which we could never do at scale before," he said.
 The future of the Navigator
 The tool lives in the AICPA's private LLM on its Azure platform, so none of the data is shared elsewhere.
 "When you're in on the chat, that chat is private only to you," Hood explained. "So your chat under your email or whatever you register with, that will stay yours and you can delete it at the end of a session, or you can keep it so you can go back in and see your prior chats and then continually update them. We will be able to look across all those chats to look at trends and all that stuff, but we can't get the specifics of your chat system."
 The AICPA is interested in tracking trends in the sort of questions users ask.
 "That's going to be probably one of the richer data sets we get, because as people begin to go in there and ask it, they're going to change their prompt as they see what's coming out of it," he said. "We're going to use it to look at how we should be thinking about how we serve our members. So it will turn into what we think about for AICPA products and services across the world."
 Another 1,500 accountants have added their insights to the LLM since the Navigator was released, and the AICPA also plans to add many of their own resources to the LLM, including their proprietary research, white papers from their technology affiliate, CPA.com, and much more. Hood said they're not currently planning to update the tool with regular iterations of the visioning exercises, but will keep an eye out for big developments that may require rethinking where accounting is headed.
 "It'll be more driven by what's happening in the environment," Hood said. "So, with major tectonic-type shifts — 'OK, let's get disciplined and go collect that data around the world again and update where we are.' Or we would keep watching what members are asking about. That could be another signal that things are starting to shift. … We not only have the trends and opportunities, but we have what members are thinking about them relative to those opportunities, predictable problems and things like that. So that means you've got this based on all the experience and wisdom of all of us global members in that data."
 In the end, he concluded, "It goes back to my favorite quote, from Sir Isaac Newton — 'If we see further, it's because we stand on the shoulders of giants.' Well, this is the first time we actually can literally stand on the shoulders of our entire profession and look out really, really far based on all that knowledge and wisdom that we're capturing."
 Both the Rise 2040 report and the Rise Navigator are available online at Rise2040.com .
